events.name: China floods (Yangtze and Huai basins) (1931)
events.best: ≈2 million (National Flood Relief Commission, 1933, drowning plus famine)
events.headline: A drought, a snowy winter and a summer of storms merged three flood seasons into one. About 180,000 km² went under water; the deaths came first from drowning and then, for a year, from disease and hunger.

events.name: Yellow River flood (1887)
events.region: Henan and the North China Plain
events.best: At least 930,000 (compilations)
events.headline: After days of heavy rain, the Yellow River broke out of the dikes that held it above the plain near Zhengzhou and spread across about 130,000 km² of farmland.

events.name: Bhola cyclone (1970)
events.best: At least 224,000 counted by survey (Lancet, 1972); ≥300,000 widely accepted
events.headline: The deadliest tropical cyclone on record. A storm surge of about 10 m arrived near high tide on the low islands of the Ganges Delta at night.

events.name: Coringa cyclone (1839)
events.region: Coringa, Godavari delta, Andhra Pradesh, India
events.best: ≈300,000 in popular compilations; no contemporary count found
events.headline: A cyclone and a storm surge often put at 12 m destroyed the port of Coringa, which never recovered. The famous 300,000 toll cannot be traced to a contemporary count.

events.name: Backerganj cyclone (1584)
events.region: Bakerganj coast (Barisal and Patuakhali), present-day Bangladesh
events.best: ≈200,000 from Mughal-era chronicles
events.headline: A five-hour storm described in Mughal-era chronicles drowned the coast of Bakla (Bakerganj); only well-built temples were said to survive.

events.name: Great Backerganj (Bengal) cyclone (1876)
events.ranking_toll: About 200,000 including epidemic and famine deaths
events.best: ≈100,000 drowned plus ≈100,000 in the famine and epidemic that followed
events.headline: A storm surge put at up to 12 m swept the islands of the Meghna estuary at night; about half the deaths came afterwards, from hunger and disease.

events.name: Chittagong cyclone (1897)
events.region: Chittagong and Kutubdia Island, present-day Bangladesh
events.best: ≈14,000 in the storm plus ≈18,000 from the cholera that followed (contemporary reports)
events.headline: Contemporary reports put the deaths at about 14,000 in the storm and 18,000 more from cholera. The 175,000 figure in rankings is several times higher and poorly sourced.

events.name: Typhoon Nina and the Banqiao dam disaster (1975)
events.best: Official ≈26,000; provisional Henan figure 85,600; up to 230,000–240,000 including famine and disease
events.headline: The remnants of Typhoon Nina stalled over Henan and dropped more than a year's rain in a day. Banqiao and 61 other dams failed, sending a wall of water across the plain at night.

events.name: Yangtze River flood (1935)
events.region: Middle Yangtze: Hubei, Hunan and neighbouring provinces
events.best: ≈145,000 drowned (plus later famine deaths)
events.headline: Torrential July rain on the Han and Li tributaries sent record flows into the middle Yangtze, breaking dikes across six provinces only four years after 1931.

events.name: Bangladesh cyclone (Cyclone 02B, 'Gorky') (1991)
events.best: At least 138,866
events.headline: As strong as a Category 5 hurricane at peak, it struck south of Chittagong near high tide. Warnings and shelters saved many lives compared with 1970, but not enough.

events.name: Cyclone Nargis (2008)
events.best: 84,537 dead and 53,836 missing (official post-disaster needs assessment)
events.headline: An unusual eastward track took a rapidly intensifying cyclone straight into the low, crowded Irrawaddy Delta, where the surge ran about 40 km inland. The military government then restricted foreign aid for weeks.

events.name: St. Felix's flood (1530)
events.best: 'More than 100,000 reportedly killed' (no primary count)
events.headline: A North Sea storm surge on 5 November 1530, 'Evil Saturday', swept away much of Zeeland and Flanders, including the land around Reimerswaal, which was never recovered.

events.name: North Sea flood (1099)
events.region: England (Thames estuary) and the Low Countries
events.best: No contemporary count; the chronicle gives none
events.headline: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records a great sea flood on 11 November 1099 but gives no death toll. The 100,000 figure appears only in modern lists.

events.name: Swatow (Shantou) typhoon (1922)
events.best: ≈5,000 in the city (contemporary report) plus ≈50,000 in the surrounding area; above 60,000 per NOAA
events.headline: A strong typhoon with a central pressure of 932 hPa or lower drove a surge of at least 3.7 m into Shantou and the surrounding coast at night.

events.name: European summer heat waves (2003)
events.best: More than 70,000 excess deaths in 16 countries (Robine et al., 2008)
events.headline: A persistent high-pressure block over a drying continent produced Europe's hottest summer on record at the time. Most of the dead were elderly people indoors, many of them alone.

events.name: St. Lucia's flood (1287)
events.region: Holland, Friesland, East Frisia and eastern England
events.best: '50,000' in chronicles; the 80,000 upper figure is unsourced
events.headline: A storm tide on 13–14 December 1287 overran dikes from Friesland to Norfolk, redrew the Dutch coastline and opened the way for the Zuiderzee.

events.name: Hakata Bay typhoon (the 'kamikaze') (1281)
events.region: Imari and Hakata bays, Kyushu, Japan
events.best: Chronicles describe the loss of most of a southern fleet reported at 100,000 troops; no count
events.headline: A typhoon wrecked the Mongol–Yuan invasion fleet anchored off Kyushu in 1281. Underwater archaeology at Takashima has since found the ships and their anchors.

events.name: European summer heat waves (2022)
events.best: 61,672 heat-related deaths (Ballester et al., 2023)
events.headline: Europe's hottest summer on record at the time brought repeated heat waves from Spain to the UK. An epidemiological study of 35 countries attributed about 61,700 deaths to the heat.

events.name: Bengal (Midnapore) cyclone (1942)
events.type: Tropical cyclone, storm surge and floods
events.best: 14,443 deaths in the storm and the following week (Government of Bengal) plus at least 1,100 from disease
events.headline: A wartime cyclone and tidal surge devastated Midnapore and destroyed much of the rice crop, one of the triggers of the Bengal famine of 1943.

events.name: Calcutta cyclone (1864)
events.region: Calcutta (Kolkata) and the Hooghly estuary, India
events.best: More than 60,000 (Gastrell and Blanford's official report, 1866)
events.headline: A cyclone drove a storm surge up the Hooghly River into Calcutta, wrecking most ships in the port. It was one of the disasters that preceded the founding of the India Meteorological Department.
